note: Complete-fit comparison for the alias-representative change, required by AGENTS.md for performance-sensitive work.  SYMMETRIC: one complete fit per side, fresh interpreter each, so the ru_maxrss high-water mark covers the same work on both -- `peak_rss_measures_fits` and `ru_maxrss_unit` record that rather than leaving it to be inferred.  BLAS pools are sampled from a background thread WHILE the fit runs, with a dwell count per configuration, because presence alone cannot distinguish a brief startup window from a phase that held.  Taken with the CPU lock held on an otherwise idle box: the 1-minute load average was read immediately before and after each timed side and sits in each side's `loadavg_one_minute` rather than in a footnote.  Every earlier revision of this file was taken under load averages in the teens or higher, and `history` lists all five measurements of this comparison beside the load each was taken under, because the spread between them tracks the machine, not the code.

summary.blas_note: An earlier revision of this file claimed the baseline spent part of the fit single-threaded and the branch did not.  That is WITHDRAWN.  `num_threads` from threadpoolctl is the configured limit (openblas_get_num_threads), not the number of threads a kernel elects to use, so it cannot show OpenBLAS running a small decomposition on one thread -- the reading only moves when something calls threadpool_limits, and in this package that is `solver_blas_threads()` capping to 1 on fit entry and `allow_wide_design(p)` releasing the cap once p >= 1500.  With p = 1680 the cap is released mid-fit by design.  Dwell counting shows exactly that: the capped configuration accounts for 2 of 224 samples on the branch side and 0 of 12219 on the baseline side, and which side catches the window is sampling luck rather than a property of either algorithm.
summary.speedup_note: No single multiplier is published.  Five runs of this comparison produced five ratios, and the spread tracks the 1-minute load average each was taken under, not the code -- the per-run ratios sit in `history` beside their load context, and only run 5 was taken on a quiet box with the load recorded immediately before and after each timed side.  The claim the runs support is that the fit is tens of times faster on this branch.
